source.title: Effect of Pulse Current and Pre-annealing on Thermal Extrusion of Cu in Through-Silicon Via (TSV)

conditions.bath: 1 M CuSO4 + 1.9 mM HCl, pH 0.5 adjusted with H2SO4, 100 ppm suppressor (CuSupH-1, commercial)
conditions.vias: 5 um dia x 60 um deep (AR12), SiO2/Ta barrier/Cu seed
conditions.pulse: peak 450 mA/cm2 fixed, on-time 2 us fixed, off-time varied to set average

DC.outcome: best DC: void-free bottom-up, linear fill, complete < 200 s

PC.outcome: best PC: highest fill ratio, no bumps; slower start (suppressor re-adsorption in off-time), steeper linear slope from 200 s on
insufficient suppressor supply in via (short off-time); pinch-off voids at very high peak j

data.fill_time_series_note: their Fig 4 shows fill fraction vs t curves: DC 1 mA/cm2 linear to completion <200 s; PC 3 mA/cm2 lower initially, steeper after 200 s. Individual points not in text - digitise Fig 4 (est. error +-0.05 fill fraction, +-10 s)

data.result: PC advantage: thinner diffusion layer (Cu2+ resupply during off-time) + suppressor re-adsorption prevents field bumps; consistent with S-NDR breakdown at via bottom

notes: Useful small-via (AR12, 5 um) DC-vs-PC validation set with a commercial suppressor at pH 0.5. Filling-ratio-vs-time curves (their Fig 4) are the digitisable time series. Supports platesim PR module qualitatively (PC outperforms DC at equal average j via suppressor resupply, not via supply of Cu2+ alone). No agitation -> lower-bound mass transfer case.
